title: Choose and order a focused idea set
instructions: Continue from the task contract and E6.2 idea pool. The chosen school-learned skill is breaking a large problem into smaller parts, and the main example is organising a school charity sale. Answer all six questions about choosing two or three supporting ideas and ordering them for the reader.

parts.prompt: Which TWO supporting ideas should be kept because they pass the relevance, development and link tests?

options.text: Before the sale, divide publicity, supplies, prices and staffing into separate tasks with deadlines.
Organisation is useful and all successful people use it.
When rain forces the stalls indoors, identify the urgent tasks, reassign helpers and check what remains.
Explain why the youth blog should use a brighter logo.

choice_rationales.A: This supplies a specific application of the selected method before the event.
choice_rationales.B: This broad claim has no bounded situation, action or evidence.
choice_rationales.C: This shows the same method working in a concrete complication and provides actions to explain.
choice_rationales.D: Blog design lies outside the task contract.

parts.hint: Keep points that develop the same learned method with a specific action and an explainable connection.
parts.correct_explanation: The initial plan and the response to rain deepen one focus through two distinct, specific applications.

parts.prompt: Why should ‘list the sale tasks’ and ‘separate the sale into publicity, supplies, prices and staffing’ be combined?

options.text: They perform the same planning job and would otherwise repeat one idea.
A composition may contain only one sentence about any event.
Specific categories are never useful in writing.
Every paragraph must discuss a different school subject.

choice_rationales.A: Both statements describe dividing the event into tasks, so they belong in one developed point.
choice_rationales.B: The limit concerns repeated ideas, not a one-sentence rule.
choice_rationales.C: The categories are useful evidence inside the combined point.
choice_rationales.D: Changing subjects would violate the prompt's one-focus boundary.

parts.hint: Ask whether the two candidates give the reader different reasoning or the same reasoning in different words.
parts.correct_explanation: Combining overlap creates space to explain one planning point with precise categories rather than pretending repetition is development.

parts.prompt: Which supporting idea should appear first?

options.text: The final reflection on why the method matters
The response to the sudden rain before the reader knows the original plan
The initial division of sale tasks and deadlines
An unrelated opinion about school fundraising

choice_rationales.A: The reflection becomes meaningful after the reader sees the evidence.
choice_rationales.B: The complication is easier to understand after the original plan is established.
choice_rationales.C: This gives the reader the context and method needed to follow the later complication.
choice_rationales.D: An unrelated opinion does not belong in the selected sequence.

parts.hint: Choose the information the reader needs before the complication and result make sense.
parts.correct_explanation: The initial plan establishes both the method and situation, so it prepares the reader for the later disruption.

parts.prompt: Which complete arrow chain gives the clearest reader-need order?

options.text: Reflection → rain response → learned method → original plan
Learned method → original plan → rain response → result and reflection
Rain response → blog design → original plan → new school subject
General slogan → second general slogan → list of subjects → conclusion

choice_rationales.A: This gives conclusions and complications before their necessary context.
choice_rationales.B: This moves from the central learning through evidence to the insight produced by that evidence.
choice_rationales.C: This sequence includes off-task material and switches focus.
choice_rationales.D: A chain of general claims provides no developed application.

parts.hint: Move from what the reader must understand to what happened and then to what the evidence shows.
parts.correct_explanation: Method, plan, complication and reflection form a clear chronological and explanatory progression.

parts.prompt: Which plan shows list planning rather than selection for depth?

options.text: Explain the method; develop the sale plan; show the response to rain; reflect on the result.
Mention mathematics, teamwork, creativity, leadership, budgeting, sport and friendship in one or two sentences each.
Combine the two descriptions of dividing tasks, then explain the concrete categories.
Use two connected moments from the same example to show the method in ordinary and difficult conditions.

choice_rationales.A: This gives each selected part a clear explanatory job.
choice_rationales.B: This multiplies topics and leaves too little space to develop any one of them.
choice_rationales.D: Two connected moments can deepen one focused example.

parts.hint: Find the plan that values the number of topics over specific explanation.
parts.correct_explanation: A rapid list of many skills breaks the single-focus scope and prevents development.

parts.prompt: Which selected plan best prepares for E6.4 while preserving one central focus?

options.text: Focus: breaking a task into parts. Point 1: plan the sale by categories and deadlines. Point 2: use the same method to adapt when rain changes the venue. Closing insight: the method makes pressure manageable.
Focuses: problem-solving, teamwork, creativity and leadership. Give one sentence to each.
Focus: charity sales. Describe food, decorations and music without explaining school learning.
Focus: a dramatic success. Invent awards and record-breaking results to impress the reader.

choice_rationales.A: The plan keeps one learned method, two distinct supporting jobs and a linked insight in a clear order.
choice_rationales.B: This switches focus and produces a shallow list.
choice_rationales.C: Event description alone does not explain transferred learning.
choice_rationales.D: Fabricated dramatic evidence is neither necessary nor honest.

parts.hint: Choose the plan with one learned method, distinct supporting jobs and a final insight earned by the evidence.
parts.correct_explanation: The focused plan selects two developable applications of the same method and orders them before the resulting reflection.
